name: NX Recall
tagline: Local conversation memory with speaker recognition and offline voice

artifacts.label: Daemon + desktop app (Linux)
artifacts.postInstallNote: Two one-time steps in a terminal: `~/.local/bin/recalld models fetch` (~500 MB of speech models — multilingual ASR — the only network use in the program), then `systemctl --user daemon-reload && systemctl --user enable --now nx-recall`. The Memory tab's local model is a separate, optional `recalld models fetch --graph` (~1.9 GB); everything else works without it and it stays switched off until you turn it on. Capture is default-deny — nothing is recorded until `recalld allow <program>`. Outside its own bin/ and lib/ this install writes exactly two files, share/systemd/user/nx-recall.service and share/applications/nx-recall.desktop, both removed on uninstall. Your transcripts and models in ~/.local/share/nx-recall are not: that directory outlives uninstall on purpose. Optional Local Voice is available in Settings: set up its local speech/voice/runtime components once (~2.1 GB download, 4 GB free), then choose a Vesktop call or local microphone and speaker. Voice inference stays local and needs no paid API.
